newsitem.title: USA: Philip Morris wants its chief protected from "harassment".
newsitem.headline: Philip Morris wants its chief protected from "harassment".

text.p: Attorneys for Philip Morris Cos. Inc. on Monday sought a protective order to prevent lawyers for Florida state from subjecting the tobacco and food giant's CEO, Geoffrey Bible, to "rude and insulting treatment" during questioning.

In a motion filed on Monday afternoon, the attorneys said they wanted the order to cover an emergency hearing scheduled before Special Master William Rutter. They want Bible to be questioned before Rutter at 1:30 p.m. EDT (1730 GMT) on Tuesday.

Rutter is assigned the task of handling motions regarding the introduction of evidence, and testimony from witnesses, by West Palm Beach Circuit Court Judge Harold Cohen in the state's $12.3 billion lawsuit against cigarette makers.
Cohen is in the middle of selecting a jury of six and nine alternates to hear testimony. The trial is scheduled to begin shortly after Labor Day.

Philip Morris attorney Stephen Krigbaum based his request on what he called the "improper" treatment given to James Morgan, chief executive officer of Philip Morris Inc., the company's subsidiary, in New York on July 31.

"Plaintiffs' counsels (Florida's attorneys) in that deposition were deplorable. This court should take action now ... by supervising the deposition and limiting its length ... to prevent a recurrence of such conduct at Bible's deposition," Krigbaum said.
When Robert Montgomery, one of the Florida's lead attorneys was called regarding the allegations, he responded:
"Every question asked was legitimate. They just don't like it. I doubt very seriously that Rutter will grant the request, but if he does, that's OK with me. I have no problem with that whatsoever."
Krigbaum in his motion accused Florida's laywers of treating "Morgan in a sarcastic, offensive demeaning fashion."
He quoted this exchange between Morgan and a Florida attorney during the deposition in support of his motion:

Q - "As far as this company (Philip Morris) is concerned, you have already disavowed any knowledge of production of the cigarette, you have disavowed any knowledge of the science of the cigarette. So it would seem that your singular function in this company is to sell the product that the company produces. Am I wrong in that regard, sir?"

Q - "This little litany that you just gave us regarding lung cancer and cigarettes, that's a selling pitch that you've structured to use in every deposition that's been taken in every lawsuit that's been filed against your company around the country, isn't it, sir?"
At this point, attorneys representing Morgan objected again to the manner in which Morgan was being questioned.

"This was not a discovery deposition; it was a five-hour harangue -- an insulting inquisition with only one purpose -- to belittle and embarrass Mr. Morgan as much as possible in front of the video camera," Krigbaum said.
"Unless this court intervenes, there is no reason to believe Mr. Bible will be treated any differently by (Florida') counsel," Krigbaum said.
